metadata.basin: Upper Assam Basin (Greater Duliajan / Nahorkatiya Block)

formations.name: Dhekiajuli / Alluvium
formations.lithology: Unconsolidated coarse sand, pebble beds, alluvial silt
formations.description: Quaternary to Pliocene unconsolidated fluvial sequence requiring high-viscosity spud mud.

formations.name: Girujan Clay
formations.lithology: Mottled plastic claystone, ferruginous silty shale
formations.description: Regional caprock composed of sticky hydro-swelling clays; requires KCl/Polymer inhibition.

formations.name: Tipam Sandstone
formations.lithology: Massive cross-bedded arkosic sandstone with thin shale bands
formations.description: Major Miocene reservoir unit in Upper Assam; high permeability sands prone to differential sticking.

formations.name: Barail Coal-Shale
formations.lithology: Interbedded fissile carbonaceous shale, fractured coal seams, channel sands
formations.description: Oligocene primary hydrocarbon producer & highest-risk drilling horizon in Nahorkatiya-Moran block. Natural micro-cleats in coal seams cause sudden circulation losses between 3,400–3,460 m.

formations.name: Kopili Shale
formations.lithology: Dark splintery marine shale, thin fossiliferous limestone streaks
formations.description: Late Eocene overpressured marine shale requiring careful ECD and pore-pressure monitoring.

events.description: Encountered natural cleat fractures in Barail coal seam at 3,428 m. Dynamic mud losses escalated rapidly from 4 bbl/hr to 15.4 bbl/hr with 1.24 sg Water-Based Mud. Pit volume dropped by 28 bbl.
events.root_cause: High Equivalent Circulating Density (ECD 1.31 sg) exceeding fracture propagation gradient of micro-cleated Barail coal bed (1.27 sg).
events.mitigation: Reduced pump flow rate from 2,150 LPM to 1,750 LPM. Spotted 25 bbl High-Concentration LCM Pill (15 ppb Medium Nut-Plug + 10 ppb Coarse Flake Mica + 8 ppb Sized CaCO3) across 3,415–3,450 m and soaked for 45 mins.
events.outcome: Dynamic losses reduced to <0.8 bbl/hr within 1.5 hours; full circulation regained and 9-5/8" liner set safely.

events.description: Erratic surface torque spikes from 24 kNm baseline up to 36.8 kNm accompanied by splintery coal cavings over shale shakers.
events.root_cause: Mechanical destabilization of interbedded Barail coal-shale lamination due to filtrate invasion prior to LCM seal.
events.mitigation: Added 2% poly-glycol lubricant and swept hole with 30 bbl high-viscosity bentonite pill; controlled ROP to 12 m/hr.
events.outcome: Torque stabilized at 25–27 kNm; wellbore cleaned without pack-off.

events.description: Sudden partial return loss of 12.8 bbl/hr while drilling Barail sandstone-coal interface at 3,412 m accompanied by SPP drop of 180 psi.
events.root_cause: Depleted sub-hydrostatic fracture network in upper Barail horizon.
events.mitigation: Pumped 20 bbl LCM pill (12 ppb Nut-Plug + 12 ppb Fine/Medium Mica + 5 ppb Graphite) and lowered MW from 1.25 sg to 1.22 sg.
events.outcome: Wellbore sealed; losses arrested to 0.5 bbl/hr.

events.description: BHA packed off at 3,430 m during wiper trip. Overpull reached 65 tonnes with standpipe pressure spiking to 3,150 psi (unable to rotate).
events.root_cause: Sloughing carbonaceous shale & coal rubble settling around 8-1/2" stabilizer after fluid loss reduced annular velocity.
events.mitigation: Worked pipe with hydraulic jar (42 tonnes downward blow) + spotted 15 bbl organic spotting fluid. Backreamed out of hole at 40 RPM.
events.outcome: String freed after 32 hours NPT; reconditioned mud with 3% KCl + asphaltic shale stabilizer.

events.description: Partial mud losses of 14.2 bbl/hr recorded at 3,405 m immediately upon entering middle Barail coal-shale member.
events.root_cause: High permeability micro-fractured coal cleat system intersecting deviated wellbore at 12.8 deg inclination.
events.mitigation: Pre-sheared 25 bbl Sized Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3 50-150 micron) + 15 ppb Mica pill spotted across loss zone.
events.outcome: Complete seal achieved in 65 minutes; zero further losses through remainder of Barail section.

events.description: Pit gain of 6.5 bbl with background gas jumping from 18 units to 142 units (C1 89%, C2 7%) at 3,790 m in Kopili transition zone.
events.root_cause: Pore pressure ramp in upper Kopili marine shale (1.31 sg equivalent) exceeding 1.26 sg mud weight.
events.mitigation: Shut in well on annular BOP (SIDPP 280 psi, SICP 340 psi). Circulated out influx using Driller's Method and weighted mud up to 1.34 sg with barite.
events.outcome: Well killed safely with zero surface incident.

events.description: Seepage to partial losses peaking at 9.6 bbl/hr between 3,438 m and 3,455 m in Barail formation.
events.root_cause: Induced thermal/pressure micro-fracturing during high pump rate hole cleaning.
events.mitigation: Continuous background addition of 6 ppb micronized cellulose fiber + 15 bbl Mica sweep.
events.outcome: Losses controlled below 1 bbl/hr without stopping drilling.

events.description: Differential sticking tendency observed at 2,780 m while stationary for directional survey (28 tonnes overpull).
events.root_cause: High overbalance (+340 psi) across high-permeability (520 mD) Tipam channel sand with thick filter cake.
events.mitigation: Pumped 15 bbl diesel-surfactant pipe-lax pill and worked string free with 18 kNm torque.
events.outcome: Pipe freed in 3.5 hours; added 4 ppb ultra-fine bridging CaCO3 to reduce API fluid loss to <4.2 ml/30min.

documents.verbatim_excerpt: 08:30 - 11:00 HRS: Drilling 8-1/2" hole in Barail Coal-Shale from 3,418 m to 3,428 m with 1.24 sg KCl-Polymer mud. At 3,428 m, encountered sudden drilling break (ROP jumped from 18.2 to 27.4 m/hr) followed by 180 psi SPP drop and dynamic mud loss of 15.4 bbl/hr into micro-cleated coal fractures. Reduced flow rate from 2,150 LPM to 1,750 LPM. Spotted 25 bbl LCM pill (15 ppb Medium Nut-Plug + 10 ppb Coarse Flake Mica + 8 ppb Sized CaCO3 150-micron) across 3,415-3,448 m. Soaked for 45 mins under 150 psi squeeze pressure. Full returns re-established; dynamic seepage <0.8 bbl/hr.

documents.author: Wellsite Geology & Drilling Engineering Directorate, OIL
documents.summary: Comprehensive Well Completion Report for Duliajan-South-087 detailing 12.8 bbl/hr mud loss at 3,412 m followed by mechanical pipe sticking (32 hrs NPT) at 3,430 m due to coal sloughing.

extracted_entities.mitigation: 20 bbl LCM Pill + Hydraulic jarring (42T) + 15 bbl Organic Spotting Fluid + 3% KCl/Asphaltene inhibition
extracted_entities.outcome: String jarred free after 32 hrs NPT; hole stabilized

documents.verbatim_excerpt: SECTION 4.3 - DRILLING HAZARDS & NPT ANALYSIS: While drilling Barail Coal-Shale at 3,412 m, partial circulation losses of 12.8 bbl/hr reduced annular velocity in the 8-1/2" section. During subsequent wiper trip at 3,430 m, splintery coal and carbonaceous shale cavings bridged around the upper stabilizer, causing immediate mechanical pack-off (65 tonnes overpull, 3,150 psi SPP). String was freed by spotting 15 bbl organic surfactant pill and downward jarring at 42 tonnes. LESSON LEARNED: In Barail horizon (3,400–3,450 m), always pre-treat mud with 6 ppb micronized LCM and asphaltic shale inhibitor prior to crossing 3,400 m to prevent filtrate-induced coal sloughing.

documents.verbatim_excerpt: LITHOLOGY & GAS LOG (3,400–3,445 m): Cuttings consist of 45% black vitreous sub-bituminous coal with orthogonal cleat planes, 35% dark grey fissile carbonaceous shale, and 20% fine argillaceous sandstone. At 3,405 m MD (3,368 m TVD), mud pit active sensor recorded 14.2 bbl/hr dynamic loss. Pumped pre-mixed 25 bbl CaCO3 (50-150 micron) + 15 ppb Mica pill; fracture network bridged effectively within 65 minutes.

documents.author: Drilling Operations Cell, Moran Extension
documents.summary: Daily Drilling Report #118 demonstrating preventive background LCM treatment in Moran-North-105 that restricted Barail mud losses to 9.6 bbl/hr with zero stuck-pipe NPT.

extracted_entities.mitigation: Continuous background 6 ppb micronized cellulose fiber + 15 bbl Mica sweep
extracted_entities.outcome: Drilled through Barail hazard zone with zero trip NPT

documents.verbatim_excerpt: 14:00 - 20:00 HRS: Based on offset correlation from W-093 and W-087, pre-treated active system with 6 ppb micronized cellulose fiber at 3,385 m prior to entering middle Barail coal seams. Observed partial losses of 9.6 bbl/hr at 3,438 m which rapidly self-healed to <1.0 bbl/hr following a 15 bbl Mica sweep. Confirmed effectiveness of pre-emptive wellbore strengthening.

documents.summary: 9-5/8" Intermediate Casing & Differential Sticking Incident Report in Tipam Sandstone at 2,780 m.

extracted_entities.mitigation: 15 bbl surfactant pipe-lax pill + low-density lightweight lead cement slurry (1.42 sg)
extracted_entities.outcome: String freed in 3.5 hrs; 9-5/8" casing cemented with 98% bond log index

documents.verbatim_excerpt: OPERATIONAL SUMMARY: Differential sticking encountered at 2,780 m across high-permeability (520 mD) Tipam sandstone due to 340 psi hydrostatic overbalance. Freed pipe using 15 bbl organic surfactant spotting fluid. Subsequent 9-5/8" casing cementing utilized fiber-laced 1.42 sg lead slurry to prevent breakdown across weak Tipam-Barail transition.

documents.author: Center of Excellence for Energy Studies (CoEES) & Oil India R&D, Duliajan
documents.summary: Geomechanical & Cleat-Permeability Study of Oligocene Barail Coal-Shale across 24 Wells in Greater Duliajan and Nahorkatiya Fields.

extracted_entities.event: Regional Cleat Fracture Loss & Wellbore Instability
extracted_entities.mitigation: Proactive Stress-Caging at 3,385 m using bimodal CaCO3 (50/150 micron) + Nut-Plug + Mica pill prior to penetrating 3,400 m coal horizon
extracted_entities.outcome: Reduces Barail non-productive time (NPT) by 74% across field trials

documents.verbatim_excerpt: EXECUTIVE FINDINGS (CoEES / OIL R&D): Statistical analysis of 24 directional wells in Block NHR-04 and NHR-05 reveals a 68% incidence of severe lost circulation (10–22 bbl/hr) and subsequent coal-packoff stuck pipe within a narrow 50-meter depth window (3,400 m to 3,450 m MD) inside the middle Barail Coal-Shale member. Because Barail coal cleats possess aperture widths of 80–220 microns, conventional bentonite mud fails to bridge until massive losses occur. Proactive wellbore strengthening ('Stress Caging') must be initiated 15 to 25 meters ABOVE the 3,400 m top—specifically at 3,380–3,390 m—by staging a 25 bbl bimodal LCM pill (15 ppb Nut-Plug + 10 ppb Flake Mica + 8 ppb Sized CaCO3) and restricting ECD below 1.28 sg.
